newsitem.title: USA: Gillette posts record results in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Gillette posts record results in quarter.

text.p: Gillette Co. Thursday reported record first-quarter profits, boosted by surging sales of its blade and razor products, Duracell batteries, and toiletries and cosmetics.
Net income rose to $283.7 million, or 51 cents a share, in the quarter, from $249.3 million, or 45 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales grew to $2.18 billion from $2.06 billion.
Boston-based Gillette also raised its quarterly dividend to 21.5 cents per common share from 18 cents.

"Despite the strong dollar, which depressed reported sales gains by 3 percentage points, and soft economic conditions in some key markets, we continued our positive momentum," said Chairman Alfred Zeien.
Gillette said its blade and razor sales in the first quarter were moderately higher, while profits rose sharply from those of a year ago.
Duracell battery sales and profits surged. First quarter sales of Braun Products edged down from the comparable period a year ago, while profits were down moderately, it said.
Toiletries and cosmetics sales rose considerably, while profits grew substantially.
Sales of stationery products declined well below the prior year's, while profits were virtually unchanged, Gillette said.
Oral-B toothbrush sales and profits for the first quarter strongly surpassed those of last year, it added.
"Gillette is a new-product machine," said Merrill Lynch analyst Deepak Raj. "Forty-one percent of Gillette's sales in 1996 came from products they didn't have five years ago."

As the developing world gets richer, it inevitably will consume more household products, and American companies have the brand names and the infrastructure to benefit from this rising tide, analysts said.
After all, Raj noted, this sector has a built-in advantage over many other groups, whose fortunes rise and fall with the business cycle.
"There is nothing better," Raj noted, "than a product that needs to be thrown away every few days."
Gillette's stock fell $1.375 to $80.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
